input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 binds Customer, not Vendor: Customer cannot engage another provider without first disclosing and matching any better offer for Vendor. That is a right of first refusal / MFC-style restraint functioning as de facto exclusivity, contrary to our preferred position of no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer, and it has no category limit, no time limit, and no exit on Vendor performance failure. It also directly conflicts with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. Deleting the clause is the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; the take-or-pay minimum in Section 2.1 reinforces the lock-in but is a volume-commitment issue handled separately.

proposal.summary: Delete Section 7.2 match/first-refusal obligation that operates as de facto exclusivity on Customer
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the requirement that Customer disclose and match competing offers before engaging another provider, as it operates as a de facto exclusivity/right of first refusal and conflicts with Section 12.3, under which Customer makes no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. If some form of preference is essential, we could consider a non-binding courtesy notice limited to a defined service category for no more than twelve months and ending automatically on any Vendor service-level or delivery failure.
